Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
• 36-year-old returned traveller with 4-day history of severe headache, subjective fever, generalized myalgias, and diffuse pruritic blanching rash.  
• No photophobia, neck stiffness, vomiting, focal neurologic signs, or respiratory symptoms.  
• Differential considerations (consistent with transcript and DDx):  
  – Dengue fever (high likelihood): classic symptom triad and recent Thailand travel with mosquito exposure.  
  – Chikungunya virus infection (moderate likelihood): similar presentation though arthralgia less prominent.  
  – Malaria (moderate likelihood): must be excluded despite atypical rash.  
  – Viral meningitis/other systemic viral illness (lower likelihood but needs exclusion due to headache + fever).  
• Clinician advised urgent in-person review today at GP hub for full physical exam, bloods, and possible hospital referral to exclude serious tropical or CNS infection.  
• Safety-netting: attend emergency services if unable to secure appointment or if symptoms worsen (e.g., non-blanching rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, confusion).  

Management Plan
-  management_plan_main_or_not_recorded  
  • Arrange same-day face-to-face assessment.  
  • Likely investigations at hub/hospital: FBC, platelets, liver enzymes, malaria smear/rapid test, dengue/chikungunya serology or PCR, blood cultures, basic metabolic panel.  
  • Symptomatic relief: continue paracetamol/ibuprofen as needed (within dosing guidelines).  
  • Hydration and rest advised.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Dengue fever – High likelihood: travel to Thailand, mosquito bites, fever, severe headache, blanching rash, myalgias.  
2. Chikungunya virus infection – Moderate likelihood: arboviral illness with fever, headache, rash; joint pains less marked here.  
3. Malaria (P. falciparum) – Moderate likelihood: endemic exposure; fever and headache common; rash atypical but cannot be ruled out.
